And several organizations, such as the center Victor-Gadbois and the home hospice society of Grand Montréal, specialize almost exclusively in the care of patients with cancer.
It is precisely that relative lack of healthcare services in Quebec that makes many specialized doctors in palliative care fear the adoption of a law that regulates euthanasia and assisted suicide.
Since October, a manifesto signed by prominent palliative care professionals, such as Dr. Balfour Mount and Dr. Bernard Lapointe, has circulated to show their opposition to such an initiative.
According to Dr. Christiane Martel, the health system of Quebec is not sufficiently competent to ensure that anyone has the right to palliative care before proceeding with euthanasia.
"Recently", says, "I have seen a patient pass 14 days in Emergency Department suffering great pain without the necessary measures to relieve her.
I fear that the patients wish to die alone because they are not receiving the appropriate care.
Likewise, many oncologists persist with their patients until the last day, despite the worst prognoses.
Hélène Richard's chances of survival were already at their lowest when she stopped taking an exhausting chemotherapy treatment.
"When I told my oncologist that I wanted to stop the treatment, she said that she was very sorry that I wanted to give up fighting," says.
"However, she had told me that there was nothing else to do!"
There are no all-powerful.
Dr. Martel believes that 90% of the sick who request to die appreciate their caregivers who did not attend to them in their requests once their pain has been alleviated by a palliative care team.
However, it must be said that palliative care is not absolutely effective in the treatment of pain.
According to Elsie Monereau, Director of the Home Palliative Care Services of Grand Montréal, patients do not respond to pain treatments in 8% of cases.
At the end of life, the doctors usually resort to palliative sedation, which serves to put the patient to sleep until the moment of their death, either sporadically or permanently.
We cannot pretend that we do not understand that part of the suffering.
More and more, the disease not alleviated will have the possibility of having that palliative sedation.
The sick who are not relieved say the same thing: "I want to die."
But that does not necessarily mean "I want euthanasia", but "I want that I am relieved".

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
Everything is the opposite of the current exchange rates, based on central banks, the identified transactions and the processing charges between the parties.
Moreover, as is often the case with technologies, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, created by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency that can be converted to dollars, euros, etc., and a secure protocol of exchange in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files between equal parties.
Over 200,000 transactions have been recorded thanks to 15,000 computers on the network.
And near a thousand websites accept Bitcoin as donations or as a form of payment.
The price of Bitcoin, after reaching $30 (€23) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are listed on the Bitcoincharts.com page).
It is nothing impressive when compared with the global changes in real currency or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in him in an article published in October on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "that competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional currencies".
Bitcoin differs from other virtual currency systems such as the "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be earned by playing or bought (even in some cases to exchange).
The social media site Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the network nodes are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers, and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually carried out between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public accounting book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution to the solution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a kind of temporary central bank, will have the privilege of adding that additional line.
This is a phase of file shredding, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that provides a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once the number is found, the other nodes will easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indestructibly linked to the chain of the other transactions; any modification would change the fingerprint.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be given 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible up to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also shown in each increase in the computing power.
The life of the network has already its ups and downs.
The websites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from storage.
"The decision made does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But cash money presents the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject these payments.
Others, such as the WordPress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the accounting book and showed that nearly 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "big sales" were launched.
"They changed 30,000 dollars", says Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that coin, believes quite a bit in the potential of this technology as well as in the transaction network.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate the transactions, which thus become cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain in the anonymity.
The system is easy to set up in the stores, which do not need to install new terminals or software.
Pierre Noizat says that if you just give a direction that a telephone can "photograph and recognize", it's enough, and he says he has thousands of users.
There is a general movement for review of the hierarchical systems by more horizontal systems.
"It will take time for Bitcoin to take over, but in 2013 it could change," predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will re-evaluate the various risks, which are currently considered high, in the event that this currency succeeds.

A Republican strategy to block Obama's re-election
The republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight against electoral fraud.
In any case, the Brennan Center considers this last one a myth and states that the electoral fraud is less frequent in the United States than the number of people who die from lightning strikes.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States in ten years.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, these measures will weaken the American democratic system to some extent.
In contrast to what happens in Canada, the American states are responsible for the organization of the federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of the American governments promulgated, starting from 2009, new laws that made it more difficult to register or vote.
This phenomenon has spread since the November 2010 elections, which saw the increase of 675 new Republican representatives in 26 states.
Therefore, in 2011, 180 bills were introduced that restricted the exercise of the right to vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require voters to present a photo ID, in addition to a proof of American citizenship.

On the other hand, these laws reduce the periods of advance voting, invalidate the right to register as a voter on the day of the vote and remove their right to vote from citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 elections, no American state required voters to present a photo ID.
The State of Indiana was the first to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed in 2008 the constitutionality of the Indiana law.
Therefore, the republican authorities rushed to extend that practice to other states.
In the last years, these authorities have supported legislation in 34 states to require voters to present a photo ID.
It is important to note that, unlike in Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal form of identification, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of the American citizens, that is, 21 million people of voting age, do not have any photographic ID issued by a government agency of their state.
On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 lack an identity document with those characteristics.
However, the cost of the required ID document is often more than one hundred dollars.
In this way, the new restrictions disproportionately affect the young, minorities, and people with low incomes.
In fact, 25% of African Americans, 15% of people earning less than $35,000 a year, 18% of citizens over 65 years old and 20% of the voters between 18 and 29 years old do not have a
And there is more.
In many states, the voters who vote for the Democratic candidates cannot use the photo ID issued by their institution.
On the other hand, those same states authorize the members of the fishing and hunting clubs that usually vote for the Republican parties to use the documents issued by those clubs.
Before 2004, no state required the citizenship test for voting.
Arizona was the first state to present such a requirement.
Since 2011, a dozen of states have adopted laws requiring voters to show that they are citizens of the United States.
Those measures clearly aim to limit the Hispanic vote.
It seems that two out of three Hispanic voters support the Democratic Party.
On the other hand, the Republican legislators supported certain laws that abolished the registration of voters on the same day of the election in eight states.
In addition, they limited the right of people and groups to create an assistance service for those who wished to register.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, in the 2004 general elections, the voter registration campaigns contributed to the registration of around 10 million citizens.
The measures taken since 2009 have resulted in the number of new voters in 2010 being lower than in 2006.
In addition, the Republican legislators passed laws in other five states that favored the reduction of the voting period in advance.
For example, in the 2008 elections in Florida, 33% of the voters who voted early were African Americans, while these last were only 13% of the voters in the state.
In the case of Hispanics, it happened exactly the same.
These represent only 11% of the voters, which is equivalent to 24% of the voters who vote in advance.
However, the whites, who represent 76% of the electorate, do not represent more than 46% of the voters.
Naturally, the Democratic legislators and their supporters have opposed vigorously the adoption of laws that restrict the registration of voters.
In this sense, the Democratic governors have blocked several laws.
The United States Attorney General intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
It was possible to limit the damage.
For example, only 16 out of 34 states have adopted the law requiring the presentation of an identity document with a photograph.
However, it is undeniable that the new rules adopted will complicate the exercise of the right to vote in 2012.
The Democratic critics denounce the partisan character of the laws that have been voted, since it is clear that with them the intention is to influence the results of 2012 in the key states.
A report by the Brennan Center shows that states that have adopted these laws represent 171 of the 270 votes needed to win the presidency.
It is too early to say with certainty whether these legislative changes at the level of the electoral system will have a significant impact on the results of the 2012 presidential elections.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, the measures will damage the American democratic system to some extent.
Detection of prostate cancer: Should one get a test or not?
In fact, the PSA test can give false negative or false positive results, which can lead to unnecessary medical interventions.
It is a reason more than enough to make doubt the men, who are already reluctant, about whether they should take the tests.
Should I take the test or not?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a high level of infection was detected in the sample groups, so it is difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
In addition, the European study showed a certain mortality difference between the patients who had undergone the test and those who had not.
The study, with a 12-year follow-up, showed that there is a 30 to 40% chance of developing metastases if the test of detection is not performed.
Therefore, I recommend the test starting at 50 years of age, or at 40 years of age if the father has suffered prostate cancer.
The men of African descent have a higher risk.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer is detected.
There are aggressive cancers and others that are slow-growing.

It is truly necessary to make the patient understand the level of risk of his cancer. All possible options must be offered to the patient and not necessarily to treat the prostate cancers that do not pose a long-term threat, in which case it is better to opt for active surveillance of the disease.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated, because the cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a risk to their life.
In place of that, we suggest active monitoring of the disease and, if it progresses, we offer a treatment.
We have decided more and more frequently criteria for deciding who should or should not be treated.
I recommend that the test be done anyway.
But it is important to speak with his doctor to determine whether he should take the test or not.
Movember has created, in collaboration with the International Urological Society, a tool that allows to evaluate the pros and cons of the PSA test.
This document can be downloaded (for the moment only in English, but translations will be offered soon) at the following address: http://ca.movember.com/fr/mens-health/prostate-cancer-screening
Preventing the disease
Unfortunately, there is no miracle cure for cancer.
Despite the progress of the investigations, the adoption of healthy lifestyle habits still remains the best way to reduce the risk of suffering from the disease.
We estimate that if everyone ate well and moved sufficiently, 30% of the cancers could be prevented.
"If no one smoked, that rate would have increased to at least 50%", said André Beaulieu, spokesperson for the Canadian Cancer Society.
In contrast, we evaluate that about 10% of cancers are hereditary.
Many others are completely inexplicable.
For the Canadian Cancer Society, the fight against smoking continues to be a priority despite the decrease in the number of smokers.
Tobacco is linked to 85% of lung cancer cases.
It also constitutes a risk factor for other types of cancer.
It greatly harms the health of people.
"Today, still, there are 1.5 million smokers in Quebec", said the spokesperson André Beaulieu.
A hopeful data: 10 years after quitting smoking, the risk of dying from cancer is cut in half.
The peso
Fat and obesity also favor the appearance of the disease, according to the SCC.
The risk of breast, colon, rectum, esophagus, and uterus cancer increases.
"The investigations show that regular physical activity throughout life protects against breast cancer", they add.
Food
The organization also recommends limiting the consumption of red meats.
In large quantities, they increase the risk of developing colorectal cancer.
The products of the meat industry must be avoided.
The preservation of meat for smoking, drying or curing may produce cancer-causing substances.
"They can damage the organism's cells and lead to the development of cancer", they explain.
The vitamins
In recent years, several scientists have studied the links between the vitamin complexes and cancer.
However, at the moment, their investigations are not conclusive.
According to the SCC, the studies on vitamin E are contradictory.
While in one of them the risk of prostate cancer was reduced, in the other it was increased.
The effect of vitamin D on cancer has not been determined clearly.
On the other hand, M. Beaulieu insists on the importance of talking to each person's doctor about their concerns and family history.
"Doing the test does not cause cancer."
The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the possible discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great shock last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed that this boson is a participant in the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

And what is more, it is the particle whose existence was predicted by the standard model: our best or "least bad" explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been observed empirically.
But for the physicists it is not yet clear whether it is the Higgs boson.
We know for sure that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.

With Bitcoin, all the network nodes are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers, and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually done between two electronic addresses in the form of email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes to the public accounts are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a kind of temporary central bank, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
This is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, a transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inseparably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (within ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will carry 50 bitcoins.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
Nothing in the current monetary exchanges, based on central banks, identified transactions, and processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technologies, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, created by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is a virtual currency that can be converted to dollars, euros, etc., and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files between equal parties.
Over 200,000 transactions have been recorded through 15,000 computers on the network.
And near a thousand websites accept Bitcoin as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a high of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are quoted on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is nothing impressive when compared with the world's monetary changes or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (BCE) has taken an interest in him in an article published in October on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "that competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional currencies".

Bitcoin differs from other virtual currency systems such as the "credits" used in a video game, which can be used to advance in a video game and can be earned by playing or purchased (even in some cases can be exchanged).
Facebook, the social network, also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and makes the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the network nodes are at the same time custodians of accounting books, verifiers, issuers of currency, buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, thereby ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the file, it is also possible to assume that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public accounting book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event is to write this new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a sort of central bank provisional, will be able to add that extra line.
This is a phase of file shredding, that is, of transforming a large file into a shorter and unique numeric fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that provides a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes will easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indestructibly linked to the chain of sets of the other transactions; any modification would change the fingerprint.

If, in order to commit a fraud, a user wanted to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions as valid; the other would be orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be given 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible up to the hundred millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase of the calculation power.
The life of the network has already its highs and lows.
The websites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from storage.
"The decision made does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who recently launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also considers the possibility of anonymous money through this service.
But cash money presents the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject these payments.
Others, such as the WordPress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the accounting book and showed that nearly 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "Big Sales" were launched.
"They changed 30,000 dollars", Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, who converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a bit in the potential of this technology as well as in the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate the transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, applies for his identity and thus can remain in anonymity.
The system is easy to set up in the stores, which do not need to install new terminals or software.

Pierre Noizat says that the users are millions, and that he has a system that can recognize the phone's image, and that the users can just give a direction to a phone that can "photograph and recognize".
There is a general movement for the review of hierarchical systems to more horizontal systems.
"It will take a while for Bitcoin to take over, but in 2013 there could be a change," predicts.
On the other hand, in his report, the ECB will re-evaluate the various risks, which were considered high today, in case this currency succeeds.

It is a new double or the President of Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which grants him provisional full powers, he decided to play the whole for the whole.
The world was surprised on Wednesday when the Head of State announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote on his final text the next day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State had given two more months to this Assembly to finish its work.
And for almost two years, Egypt has been using a provisional text, repeatedly modified, which weakens institutional stability and leads to judicial disputes.
This new initiative has only increased the fracture in the country.
For its opponents, the president persists in his "autocratic delirium" and continues "betraying his word" and "stepping on the right".
On the part of its supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to accelerate the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to resign from their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.
For the president, it is also a way of recovering popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy is causing unrest throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American magazine Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted on with great speed, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "Vote my text or I will keep the full powers: powers that supposedly will be abolished with the adoption of the Constitution."
It was in this strange atmosphere in which 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, most of whom are Islamist, voted the text yesterday.
Most of the liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not defend their views.
The representatives of human rights, religious minorities, and civil society also marched.
In order to achieve the necessary quorum, at dawn yesterday, 11 substitute members were added on the spot.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brothers.
As expected, the articles voted on were passed unanimously.

The commentators are amused by the fact that one of the few disagreements of the day has been expressed practically at the time of prayer, so much so that several members of the committee thought the Constituent's clock was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, which has been the subject of all eyes, is finally identical to the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia are the main source of law."

The Salafist parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental reclamation, expected that the "principles" could be replaced by "the rules", which would have allowed for a more strict application.
For the Islamic group, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and their respect for the other components of Egyptian society.
The liberals call him hypocrisy and consider that he is only a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer especially to Article 220, which grants the Al-Azhar University a consultative role, particularly for anyone who is to confirm their compliance with the laws of Sharia.
According to the Egypt expert Sophie Pommier, it is worrying because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy."
Here we present the premises of a theocracy.
The liberal fears are also increased by the fact that the next university's rector will be much less moderate than the current one.
"At the moment, there is no concrete religious involvement.
With this Constitution, we are in the civil state.

But he acknowledges that there may be some ambiguity in article 220, since the terms used imitate the religious vocabulary.
"We refer to the specific term iqh [Islamic jurisprudence, ndlr].
The question that might be asked in the future would be in what measure the civil judges are competent to speak on behalf of this.
Beyond its religious character, the text voted yesterday has received many criticisms that refer to the powers extended to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brothers will claim that they are few compared to those during the previous regime.
Another contentious point: the powers granted to the military.
According to the desire of the military, the review of the Defense Budget will not be submitted to the Parliament, but to a National Defense Council.
Neither will civilian trials be held in military courts, as the human rights associations had demanded.
These also showed their concerns regarding the text, which they consider a death sentence.
The crime of blasphemy continues, and from now on, insults are prohibited, which could lead to serious consequences for freedom of expression, especially for the press.
In addition, no article emphasizes the protection of women, says Heba Morayef, of Human Rights Watch.
According to her, the only positive thing is the prohibition of torture according to Article 36.

However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional currencies".
Bitcoin is different from other virtual currencies such as the "credits" used in a video game and that can be earned by playing or even exchanged (even in some cases).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the network nodes are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers, and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is done in reality between two email addresses.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double key system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes to the public accounts are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a kind of central bank, will have the privilege of adding that line.
This is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, a transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique fingerprint.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inseparably linked to the other transactions; any change would change the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (within ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will carry 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the cent, which leaves a wide margin.

A Republican strategy to block Obama's re-election
The Republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight against electoral fraud.
Now, the Brennan Center considers this last one a myth and claims that the number of people killed by lightning is less than the number of people killed in the United States by lightning.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States in ten years.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In that sense, these measures will weaken the American democratic system.
In contrast to Canada, the states are responsible for the organization of the federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of the American governments promulgated, starting from 2009, new laws that made it difficult to register or vote.
This phenomenon has spread since the November 2010 elections, which saw the increase of 675 new Republican representatives in 26 states.
Therefore, in 2011, 180 bills were introduced that restricted the right to vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require voters to present a photo ID, as well as a proof of American citizenship.

On the other hand, these laws reduce the period of advance voting, invalidate the right to register as an elector on the day of the vote and remove the right to vote from citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 American elections, no state required voters to present a photo ID.
The State of Indiana was the first to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed in 2008 the constitutionality of the Indiana law.
Therefore, the Republican authorities hurried to extend that practice to other states.
In the last years, these authorities have supported 34 laws to force voters to present a photo ID.
It is important to note that, unlike in Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal identity document, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of the American citizens, that is, 21 million people of voting age, do not have any photographic identification issued by a state agency.
On the other hand, five million voters in 2012 lack a document of those characteristics.
However, the cost of the required identification document is more than one hundred dollars.
In this way, the new restrictions affect disproportionately the young, the minorities, and the low-income people.
In fact, 25% of the Afro-American population, 15% of those earning less than 35,000 dollars a year, and 20% of the voters between 18 and 29 years old do not have a photo ID.
And there is more.
In many states, the voters who vote for the Democratic candidates cannot use the photo ID issued by their institution.
On the other hand, those same states authorize the members of the fishing and hunting clubs to use the documents issued by those clubs.
Before 2004, no state required the test of citizenship to vote.
Arizona was the first state to present such a demand.
Since 2011, a dozen of states have adopted laws requiring voters to show that they are American citizens.
Those measures clearly aim to limit the Hispanic vote.
It seems that two out of three Hispanics support the Democratic Party.
On the other hand, the Republican legislators supported certain laws that abolished the registration of voters on the same day of the vote in eight states.
Furthermore, they limited the right of people and groups to create an assistance service for those who wished to register.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, in the 2004 general elections, the registration of voters contributed to the registration of around 10 million citizens.
The measures taken since 2009 have resulted in the registration of new voters dropping to 2010 compared to 2006.
In addition, the Republican legislators adopted laws in five other states that favored the early voting period.
For example, in the 2008 Florida elections, 33% of the voters who voted early were African Americans, while these latter were only 13% of the voters in the state.
In the case of the Hispanics, it was exactly the same.
These represent only 11% of the voters, which is equivalent to 24% of the voters who vote early.
However, the voters, who represent 76% of the electorate, do not represent more than 46% of the voters who vote early.
Obviously, the Democratic legislators and their supporters have opposed the adoption of laws that restrict the registration of voters.
In this sense, the Democratic governors have blocked several laws.
The United States Attorney General intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
It was possible to limit the damage.
For example, only 16 of 34 states have adopted the law requiring the presentation of an identity document with a photograph.
However, it is undeniable that the new rules adopted will complicate the voting rights in 2012.
The Democratic critics accuse the laws that have been voted on of being partisan, since it is clear that with them the results of 2012 in the key states are to be influenced.
A report from the Brennan Center shows that the states that have adopted these laws represent 171 of the 270 votes needed to win the presidency.
It is too early to say with certainty whether these legislative changes at the electoral system will have a significant impact on the results of the 2012 presidential elections.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, the measures will weaken the American democratic system.
Cancer of the prostate: Should one take the test or not?
In fact, the PSA test presents false results, which may lead to unnecessary medical interventions.
It is a reason more than enough to doubt the men, who are already reluctant, whether they should be tested.
To take the test or not?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a large number of cases were detected, so it is difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
In addition, the European study showed a certain mortality difference between the patients who had been tested and those who had not.
The study, with a 12-year follow-up, showed that there is a 30 to 40% chance of having metastatic disease if the test has not been performed.
Therefore, I recommend the test from the age of 50, or from the age of 40 if the father has had prostate cancer.
The African-American men have a higher risk.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer is detected.
There are aggressive cancers and other cancers that are lazy.

It is truly necessary to make the patient understand the degree of risk of his cancer. All possible options must be offered and not necessarily the prostate cancers, in which case active surveillance should be preferred.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated, since the cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a risk to their life.
In place of that, we suggest active monitoring of the disease and, if it progresses, we offer a treatment.
We have decided with more frequency the criteria for deciding who should or should be treated.
I recommend that the test be done in any case.
But it is important to speak with his doctor to determine whether he should take the test or not.
Movember has created, in collaboration with the International Urology Society, a tool that allows to evaluate the pros and cons of the PSA test.
This document can be downloaded (at the moment only in English, but will be offered in Spanish soon) at the following address: http://ca.movember.com/fr/mens-health/prostate-cancer-screening
To prevent the disease
Unfortunately, there is no miracle cure for cancer.
Despite the progress of the investigations, the adoption of healthy lifestyles still remain the best way to reduce the risk of disease.
We estimate that if everyone eats well and moves sufficiently, 30% of the cancers could be prevented.
"If no one smoked, that rate would increase to 50%", said André Beaulieu, spokesperson for the Canadian Cancer Society.
In contrast, we evaluate that around 10% of cancers are hereditary.
Many others are completely inexplicable.
For the Canadian Cancer Society, the fight against smoking continues to be a priority despite the decrease in the number of smokers.
Tobacco is linked to 85% of lung cancer cases.
It also constitutes a risk factor for other types of cancer.
It greatly harms the health of the people.
"Today, still 1.5 million smokers are in Quebec", said the spokesperson André Beaulieu.
A hopeful fact: 10 years after quitting smoking, the risk of dying of cancer is halved.
The peso
Fat and obesity also favor the appearance of the disease, according to the SCC.
The risk of breast, colon, and rectum cancer, as well as of the stomach and uterus, increases.
"The research shows that regular physical activity throughout life protects against breast cancer", they add.
The food
The organization recommends, also, to limit the consumption of red meats.
In large quantities, they increase the risk of developing colorectal cancer.
The cured meats must be avoided.
The preservation of the meat for curing, drying or salting may cause the formation of carcinogenic substances.
"They can damage the organism and lead to the development of cancer", we explain.
The vitamins
In the last years, several scientists have studied the links between vitamins and cancer.
However, at the moment, the investigations are not conclusive.
According to the SCC, the studies about vitamin E are contradictory.
While in one of them, a decrease in the risk of prostate cancer was observed, in the other, a more significant increase was noted.
The effect of vitamin D on cancer has not been determined clearly.
On the other hand, M. Beaulieu insists on the importance of talking about each person's family history and their medical conditions.
"Testing for the detection of cancer does not cause cancer."
The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the possible discovery of the Higgs boson caused a great shock last summer, and for a reason.
It is believed that this boson is the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

And what is more, it is the particle whose existence was predicted by the standard model: our best or "less bad" explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been observed empirically.
But for the physicists, it is not yet clear that it is the Higgs boson.
We know without a doubt that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
Moreover, new data released this week at an important physics conference in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is needed to be completely sure.
In any case, we assume it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is about.
In this great world, there is a general and inescapable law that implies that two things cannot be found at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and do it too much, because it will end up hurting you.

Although particle physics is a very complex world, it has been shown that there is also a law of this kind: the exclusion principle, which states that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "state"; a "state" that consists, roughly, of some of its characteristics
The physicists classify the particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey the principle of Pauli.
And another are the anarchists, a dirty gang that has no respect for anything, or at least not for this principle, which means that they can be found in the same place and at the same time.

According to the Berkeley Particle Adventure website, which is extraordinary, the particles are divided into two groups: mesons, which we will not discuss, and the "force particles", which are related to the natural forces.
These are not the exotic animals that we could believe.
In fact, if he is able to read this chronicle, it is because of an extraordinary particle: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as a "message" of electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disturbs" the electromagnetic field in that environment; a little like when we throw a stone into a lake.
In this "disorder" a electromagnetic wave is born (of light, infrared, ultraviolet, etc.), and this wave is not another thing than a photon; that is, one of the bosons "carriers of force".
Most stable field
The same happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.

Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, one needs to reach extremely high energies, just as if it were a frozen lake in which only a large rock could slide across the surface.
Therefore, a huge particle accelerator, such as the one at CERN (the great particle accelerator is a ring of 27 km circumference!) is needed to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, not all the particles nor all the materials interact with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do this, but others don't: a piece of paper, for example, does not stay on the door of a refrigerator.
In the same way, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have mass, while the rest (such as the photon, for example), do not.
Now, what can those investigations contribute to the matter?, asks Mrs. Plamondon.
For the science, this is to verify the validity of the standard model (MS), and also allows physicists to examine the differences between the observations and the predictions of the MS.
On the other hand, many want to find, since the smallest difference could open a door to a new physics that covers certain holes in the model.
This, to be said, has enormous deficiencies, such as not proposing any explanation regarding the gravity (¡ups!) or the dark matter (¡otro ups!).
But we have not found such differences in the CERN so far.
Consequences
The consequences of these investigations in our daily life are difficult to predict, but we do not believe that we are wrong in saying that it will have none.
For the sake of showing: at the beginning of the 60s, the pioneers of the laser in the laboratories did not at all expect the revolution that their work would bring about.
They saw the scientific applications, but nothing more.

In fact, as the physicist Willard Boyle, who worked in the Bell Labs, where the laser was invented in 1960, and who developed the first continuous laser (the first ones were pulsed) in 1962, at the beginning the laser was considered more or less as a laboratory
Imagine...
And also, the applications can come from all the instrumentation that surrounds the research.
For example, the same Willard Boyle developed a light detector in 1969 during his research on optics.
Although it was not at all his original intention, this detector now serves as a "eye" for all digital devices, which has earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2009.
That does not mean, of course, that the LHC activities necessarily want to change our lives, but never know...
Palliative care. The best way to die... | Le Devoir
In the Quebec Commission on the End of Life, the issue of the end of life was recently debated.
The debate must be resumed soon while preparing a law.
Now, within that essential domain, there is still much to be done.
The Devoir has tried to see him in person.
Just a few weeks ago, Mr. L. lived alone in his apartment in the Montérégie.
The prostate cancer that was destroying him had given him two years of rest.
"I had five years of life, but I have been like this for seven days", he said, lying on his bed in the center of palliative care, the day before.
"But it's always a shock, we can't be prepared for this", continues.
The disease has caused a lot of problems: a great weakness that prevents him from going to the bathroom and even eating by himself.
Sitting in front of an appetizing lunch, accepts help to eat.
Brave, he even smiles, talks to the strangers who give him attention, bring him medicine and offer him a bath.
The ordinary courage.
"My greatest wish is that I be cured of the diarrhea, it is humiliating", confesses.
Hours later, the team found a remedy for that illness.
"During our lives we learn that a man makes a footstep", says Pierre Brodeur, a psychologist at the center Victor-Gadbois.
Returning to their childhood, for certain people, is an unacceptable humiliation.
"That depends on the person's ability to accept that regression", notes.
Because, according to the opinion of the majority of people who work in palliative care, the great moments occur in the heart of that regression.
All the patients who enter the palliative care center suffer from cancer.
They have a maximum life expectancy of three months.
In that state, the medical team that surrounds them no offers "restorative care".
The greatest fear of Mrs. A., 89 years old, is to die "asphyxiated".
But the disease has made him discover his children.
"I have good children", adds.
"I have no more wishes in this life", he says, before accepting that she be given a mask to help her breathe.
And wait, in the next days, a last visit of his son who lives in Italy.
In Victor-Gadbois, a group of volunteers will take care of the body and provide meals.
Care is given when nothing more can be done.
To help that his death be more comfortable.
In Quebec, we have a bed for each 11,700 residents.
It is very little, since we know that all of us will eventually die.
Here, life continues in the best possible conditions, explains Dr. Christiane Martel, one of the doctors at the center.
Either in physical, emotional, or spiritual comfort.
The dying man is given mouthwashes with brandy or Pepsi according to the request.
The diabetics are no longer controlled by their blood sugar.
Death is part of everyday life.
Last night, we served him a beer, which he died during the night.
In the morning, his son finished the beer at the feet of the deceased.
"We help both the patients and their loved ones", says Nathalie Savard, the director of the care.
In the center of Victor-Gadbois, the days pass without ever being the same.

Next to a man of 94 years who is savoring his last family reunion in the yard, a young man of 36 years old dies tragically, surrounded by his parents, his wife and his two children, after having tried everything to survive.
"Since six months, there have been three to five beds occupied by people under 45 years of age with cancer", says Dr. Christiane Martel.
53% of the patients admitted to the Victor-Gadbois Hospital come from home and 47% of the hospital.
Palliative care problem

77% of Canadians simply do not have access to palliative care, that is, care conceived to relieve suffering when a patient reaches the end of his life, whether at home, in a hospital, or in a care center.
And several organizations, such as the Victor-Gadbois Center for Palliative Care and the Montreal-based Palliative Care Society, specialize almost exclusively in the care of cancer patients.
It is precisely that relative lack of medical care in Quebec that makes many specialists in palliative care fear the adoption of a law that regulates euthanasia and assisted suicide.
Since October, a manifesto signed by prominent palliative care experts, such as Dr. Balfour Mount and Dr. Bernard Lapointe, has circulated to show their opposition to such an initiative.
According to Dr. Christiane Martel, the health system of Quebec is not sufficient to ensure that anyone has the right to palliative care before proceeding with euthanasia.
"Recently", says, "I have seen a patient suffering for 14 days in the Emergency Room without the necessary measures to relieve her.
I fear that the patients want to die alone because they are not receiving adequate care.
In parallel, many oncologists persist with their patients until the last day, despite the worst prognosis.
Hélène Richard's hopes for survival were already at their lowest when she stopped on a draining treatment.
"When I told my oncologist that I wanted to stop the treatment, she said that she was very sorry that I wanted to give up the fight", says.
However, she had said that there was nothing more to do!
There are no powerful people
Dr. Martel believes that 90% of the sick who request to die are grateful to their caregivers who did not care for them before their pain was alleviated by a palliative care team.
But it must be said that palliative care is not absolutely effective in the treatment of pain.
According to Elsie Monereau, director of the Home Care Services of Grand Montreal, 8% of the cases do not respond to the treatments for pain.
At the end of life, the doctors usually use palliative sedation, which is used to put the patient to sleep until the time of death, either sporadically or permanently.
We cannot pretend that we do not understand that part of the suffering.
The disease is not being alleviated, and it will have the possibility of having palliative treatment.
The sick who are not cured say the same thing: "I want to die".
But that does not necessarily mean "I want euthanasia", but "I want to be relieved".

Each transaction between two users is made in reality between two electronic addresses in the form of email.

A Constitution with a sword in Egypt
It is a new double or nothing with the President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which grants it provisional powers, he decided to play it all for the best.
The President was surprised by everyone on Wednesday when he announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote on the final text the next day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State had given two months more to that Assembly to finish its work.
Almost two years have passed since Egypt used a provisional text, which has been modified several times, weakening the institutional stability and leading to judicial entanglements.
This new initiative has only increased the fracture in the country.
For his opponents, the President continues to be in a delirium and continues to betray his word and to trample the rights.
On the part of its supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis and speed up the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Egyptians to abandon their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the people.
For the President, it is also a form of restoring popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy causes havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems to be convinced that Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American magazine Time.

Considering that that resource has been voted on with great speed, it contains an ultimatum to the Egyptian people: "you vote on my text or I will retain the full powers", powers that are supposed to end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It was in that strange atmosphere in which 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, mostly Muslim, voted the text yesterday.
Most of the liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not make their case.
The representatives of human rights, the religious minorities and the civil society made the same.
In order to achieve the necessary quorum, 11 substitutes were added to the list at the last minute.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.
As expected, the articles passed by unanimous vote.

The commentators are amused by the fact that one of the few disagreements of the day has been expressed at the time of prayer, and as a result, several members of the committee thought that the Constitution was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, remains finally identical to the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law".

The Salafist parties, who claim that the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental requirement, expected that the principles could be replaced by the rules, which would have allowed for a more strict application.
For the Islamic community, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and respect for the other components of Egyptian society.
The liberals accuse him of hypocrisy and consider it to be nothing but a publicity stunt.
According to them, the constitution is being Islamized through other articles.
They refer, in particular, to Article 220, which grants the Al-Azhar University a consultative role, especially for those who have confirmed their compliance with the Sharia law.
According to the Egyptian expert Sophie Pommier, it is worrying because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy."
Here we see the premises of a theocracy.
The fears of the liberals are also increased by the fact that the next university president will be much more moderate than the current one.
"At the moment, there is no concrete religious involvement.
With this Constitution, we are in the civil state.

Most of the lawyers who have worked on that text are not ulamas but university graduates, some of whom have been trained in the French system, explains Alexis Blouet, who is preparing a thesis on the constitutional transition in Egypt.
But he acknowledges that there may be some ambiguity in Article 220, since the terms used imitate the religious vocabulary.
"We refer to the term 'iqh' [Islamic jurisprudence, ndlr].
And the question that could be asked in the future would be in what degree the civil judges are competent to speak on this matter.
Beyond its religious character, the text voted yesterday has received many criticisms that refer to the powers extended to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brothers claim that they are few compared to those before the previous regime.
Another point of contention: the powers granted to the military.
According to the desire of the military, the review of the Defense budget will not be submitted to the Parliament, but to a national defense council.
Also, the military tribunals will not be allowed to be used, as the human rights organizations had requested.
These also showed their concerns about the text, which they consider to be a killing.
The crime of blasphemy remains and, from now on, insults are prohibited, which could lead to serious consequences for the freedom of expression, especially the press.
Furthermore, no article emphasizes the protection of women, says Heba Morayef, of Human Rights Watch.
According to her, the only positive thing has been the prohibition of torture according to Article 36.

The new electoral laws require voters to present a photo ID and a citizenship certificate, in addition to a citizenship certificate.

On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 lack a document of identity with those characteristics.
However, the cost of the required document is more than a hundred dollars.

200,000 transactions have been recorded thanks to 15,000 computers in the network.

The price of Bitcoin, after reaching 30 dollars (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to 2 dollars five months later, and it is now around 10 dollars (prices are listed on bitcoincharts.com).
It is not impressive when compared to the changes in real currency or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in him in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the Bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional currencies".
Bitcoin is different from other systems with virtual currencies like "credits" used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or even exchanged in some cases.
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all nodes of the network are at the same time depositaries of books, verifiers, emitters, and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is made in reality between two electronic addresses in the form of electronic mail.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is electronically signed through a double-key system.
The network can verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner will have the privilege of adding that line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique fingerprint.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that provides a particular signature (with zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the others verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inseparably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the hash.

If, in order to commit a fraud, a user wanted to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would be left without any trace, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but are divisible up to the hundred million, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.

While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which grants provisional powers, he decided to play the whole for the whole.
The President took everyone by surprise on Wednesday when he announced that the Assembly would vote on the final text tomorrow.
It has only been a week since the Head of State had given two months more to the Assembly to finish its work.
And almost two years have passed since Egypt used a provisional text, which has weakened the institutional stability and led to judicial entanglements.
This new initiative has only increased the fracture in the country.
For their opponents, the President continues to be in a delirium and continues to betray his word and to pise his right.
On the part of his supporters, it is ensured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis and accelerate the transition process.

A very short time period that forces the Brothers to renounce their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.

Mohammed Morsi seems to be convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American weekly newspaper Time.

It is in this strange atmosphere in which 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, mostly Islamic, voted yesterday.
The majority of the liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not justify their arguments.
The representatives of human rights, the religious minorities and the civil society made the same thing.

Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.

The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, remains finally identical to the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law".

The Islamic parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental claim, hoped that the principles could be replaced by the rules, which would have allowed for a more strict application.
For the Islamic community, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and respect for the other components of Egyptian society.
The liberals label him as hypocrisy and consider that it is nothing but a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer, in particular, to Article 220, which grants the Al-Azhar University a consultative role, in particular for those who have to confirm their compliance with the Sharia law.
According to the Egyptian expert Sophie Pommier, it is worrying because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy."

According to the desire of the military, the review of the Defense Budget will not be submitted to the Parliament, but to a National Defense Council.

In this great world, there is a general law that implies that two things cannot be found at the same time.

Although particle physics is a very complex world, it has been shown that there is a law of this type: the principle of Pauli, which states that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "state".
The physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find good citizens called fermions, who obey smartly at the beginning of Pauli.

In this " disorder ", a electromagnetic wave (of light, infrared, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is, one of the bosons " carriers of force".
The most stable field
The same happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "ordered" for this boson to appear.

Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, one needs to reach extremely high energies, just like a frozen lake in which only a thick rock can slide across the surface.

The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.

They saw scientific applications, but nothing more.

A Republican strategy to block Obama's re-election
The republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight against electoral fraud.

In any case, the Brennan Center considers this last statement a myth and claims that the electoral fraud is less frequent in the United States than the number of people who die each year from lightning strikes.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States in ten years.
One thing is certain: those new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In that sense, these measures will weaken the American democratic system to some extent.
In contrast to what happens in Canada, the American states are responsible for organizing the federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of American governments promulgated, starting from 2009, new laws that made it more difficult to register or vote.
This phenomenon has spread since the November 2010 elections, which saw an increase of 675 new Republican representatives in 26 states.
Therefore, in 2011, 180 bills were introduced that restricted the exercise of the right to vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require voters to present an identity document with a photograph, in addition to a proof of American citizenship.

On the other hand, those laws reduce the periods of early voting, invalidate the right to register as a voter on the day of the vote, and remove their right to vote from citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 American elections, no American state required voters to present a photo ID.
Indiana's state government was the first to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed in 2008 the constitutionality of the Indiana law.
Therefore, the Republican authorities rushed to extend that practice to other states.
In the last few years, these authorities have supported legislation in 34 states to require voters to present an ID with a photograph.
It is important to note that, unlike in Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal identity document, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of American citizens, that is, 21 million people of voting age, do not have any photographic identification issued by a government agency in their state.
On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 lack an identity document with those characteristics.
However, often the required identification document costs more than one hundred dollars.
In this way, the new restrictions affect disproportionately the young, minorities, and people with low incomes.
In fact, 25% of African Americans, 15% of people earning less than $35,000 a year, 18% of citizens over 65 years old, and 20% of voters between 18 and 29 years old do not have a
And there's more.
In many states, students and voters who vote for the Democratic candidates cannot use the photo ID issued by their institution.
On the other hand, those same states authorize members of fishing or hunting clubs that usually vote for the Republican parties to use the documents issued by those clubs.
Before 2004, no state required the citizenship test to vote.
Arizona was the first state to present such a requirement.
Since 2011, a dozen of states has adopted laws that require voters to show that they are American citizens.
Those measures clearly aim to limit the Hispanic vote.
It seems that two out of three Hispanic voters support the Democratic Party.
On the other hand, the Republican legislators supported in 2011 certain laws that abolished the registration of voters on the same day as the vote in eight states.
Moreover, they limited the right of people and groups to create an assistance service for voters who wished to register.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, in the 2004 general elections, the voter registration campaigns contributed to the registration of around 10 million citizens.
The measures taken since 2009 have resulted in the new voter registration rate falling in 2010 compared to 2006.
In addition, the Republican legislators passed laws in other five states that favored the reduction of the voting period in advance.
For example, in the 2008 elections in Florida, 33% of the voters who voted early were African American, while these latter were only 13% of the state's voters.
In the case of Hispanics, it happened exactly the same.
These represent no more than 11% of the voters, which is equivalent to 24% of the citizens who vote in advance.
However, the whites, who represent 76% of the electorate, do not represent more than 46% of the voters who vote in advance.
Naturally, the Democratic legislators and their supporters have opposed fervently the adoption of laws that restrict voter registration.
In this regard, the Democratic governors have blocked several pieces of legislation.
The United States Attorney General intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
It was, in part, possible to limit the damage.
For example, only 16 of 34 states have adopted the law requiring the presentation of an identity document with a photograph.
However, it is undeniable that the new rules adopted will complicate the exercise of the right to vote in 2012.
The Democratic critics denounce the partisan nature of the laws that have been voted, since it is clear that with them it is intended to influence the results of 2012 in the key states.
A 2011 report by the Brennan Center shows that the states that have adopted these laws represent 171 of the 270 votes needed in the electoral college to achieve the presidency.
It is too early to assert with certainty whether these legislative changes at the level of the electoral system will have a significant impact on the results of the 2012 presidential elections.
One thing is certain: those new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, the measures will damage part of the American democratic system.

In fact, the PSA test can give erroneous results, with false negatives or even false positives, after which unnecessary medical interventions are carried out.
It is a reason more than enough to make doubt the men, already reluctant, about whether they should take the detection tests.
Should I take the test or not?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a high level of infection was detected in the sample groups, so it is difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
On the other hand, the European study showed a certain mortality difference between the patients who had undergone the detection and those who had not.
The study, with a 12-year follow-up, showed that there is a 30 to 40% chance of developing metastases if the test of detection has not been performed.
Therefore, I recommend the test starting from the age of 50, or from the age of 40 if your father has suffered prostate cancer.
The men of African origin have a higher risk.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer is detected.
There are aggressive cancers and other cancers that are indolent.

It is truly necessary to make sure that the patient understands the level of risk of his cancer. All possible options should be offered and not necessarily to treat prostate cancers that do not threaten long-term life, in which case it is more appropriate to opt for active surveillance of the disease.
Today, many men who have been detected with cancer are not treated, because the cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a life-threatening risk.
In place of that, we suggest active monitoring of the illness and, if it progresses, we offer a treatment.
We have decided more and more frequently precise criteria for deciding who should or should not be treated.
I recommend that the test be done in any case.
But it is important to speak with his doctor to determine whether he should take the test or not.

Over 200,000 transactions have been recorded thanks to 15,000 computers in the network.
